units_sheet_a.prompt: {STYLE} A sprite sheet of nine game units for a top-down strategy map, repainting the units of the reference sheet in the same places, the same order and the same colours and designs: top row a Greek hoplite with a round shield and spear, a Roman legionary with a rectangular shield, a peasant militiaman with a spear; middle row a settler pushing a laden handcart, an armoured knight on a barded warhorse, a two-horse war chariot with a driver; bottom row a wooden siege catapult, an ancient trireme galley with a square sail, a medieval caravel. Every unit is seen from the same steep overhead camera, about 65 degrees above the ground, like painted miniatures on a tabletop seen from above: we see the tops of helmets and heads, shoulders, the faces of shields, horse backs, cart beds and ship decks, with only a little of the fronts. They are designed to read from above at a tiny size: big simple shapes, a strong dark outline, bright blue player colour on shields, cloaks, plumes and sails. All nine are painted at ONE shared scale, true to their real sizes relative to each other: a man on foot is small, a knight on his horse is about twice as long as a man, the chariot and its two horses and the catapult are larger still, and the two ships are the largest, each filling its own third of the sheet. Each unit faces right. {SHEET}
